subject: E2E SLO scoping for Acme Labs — next steps and test scoping
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: E2E SLO scoping for Acme Labs — next steps and test scoping

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the E2E latency qualification you asked about (hosted API vs your current provider).

Summary from our call:
- Goal: validate that Redwood Hosted meets your production p95/p99 E2E latency targets for document classification and chat endpoints under representative traffic.
- Target SLAs: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 650ms (end-to-end, from client to final token); burst concurrency up to 120 concurrent users during peak for Region: us-west.
- Current provider baseline: you mentioned p95 ~ 300ms and p99 ~ 1.1s for the same flows (thanks for the sample metrics).

Proposed test scope (high level):
1) Traffic shape: 30 min warmup + 1 hour steady-state at 60 RPS, plus 10m spike to 120 RPS. We included a tiny sample CSV of representative requests in the attachment (sample_traffic_snippet.csv).
2) Concurrency modalities: single-shot generation, streaming token-by-token, and pinned long-session calls (KV-cache heavy). We want to validate both short-lived requests (<=128 tokens) and long-context (up to 2048 tokens).
3) Metrics we will capture: client-side end-to-end latencies (p50/p95/p99), server-side token emission latency, queueing/backpressure events, success rate, and tail variance across availability zones.
4) Instrumentation: we'll provide a test harness that emits traces to your staging endpoint (no production keys). We can optionally ingest your current provider's traces for like-for-like comparison if you share them.

Action items / asks from Acme Labs:
- Share a sanitized 15–30 minute sample traffic file (CSV or JSONL) that matches your production mix (we included a tiny example).
- Confirm whether streaming must start sending tokens within X ms of request acceptance, and whether partial responses are acceptable for specific flows.
- Any network egress constraints or IP whitelisting for our test clients.

Planned timeline: once we get the sample traffic and whitelist info, we can run an initial baseline within 3 business days and deliver a short report with p95/p99 comparisons and variance heatmaps.

I've cc'd Marissa (solution lead) and Ben (performance engineering) to scope the harness and ensure we capture the right telemetry.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a scoping call tomorrow afternoon unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

Attachments: sample_traffic_snippet.csv (csv)
From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acmelabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@acmelabs.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E SLO scoping for Acme Labs — next steps and test scoping

Thanks Kimberly — that recap looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications and an initial artifact attached.

Clarifications:
- Streaming requirement: for our interactive chat flow, we need first token emitted within 250ms for most queries; beyond that, graceful degradation is acceptable (i.e., show a typing indicator).
- Long-context jobs: batch document classification runs (background) are elastic — we only need throughput guarantees for that flow (target throughput 800 docs/min at average doc size ~ 1.7k tokens). Those can be tested separately from chat.
- For security, we can whitelist the test harness IPs for staging only; will send the IP list to you shortly.

Attached: current_provider_metrics_q1.pdf — this is a sanitized extract of our RUM metrics for the last quarter (p95/p99 broken out by flow). For the sanity check, note that the p99 numbers spike at end-of-month due to billing/reporting jobs.

We'll upload a 30-minute JSONL sample of streaming and non-streaming requests to the Drive folder you listed by EOD. If you need earlier access to the trace format, let me know.

- Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Labs
daniel.lee@acmelabs.com

Attachments: current_provider_metrics_q1.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E SLO scoping for Acme Labs — next steps and test scoping

Appreciate the details, Daniel. A couple of technical notes from the performance engineering side: 

- Streaming vs non-streaming: p99 tail is often dominated by queueing and context-switches when streaming at high concurrency. For fair apples-to-apples, we should run three separate experiments: pure non-streaming, streaming with small tokens (<=64 token responses), and streaming with long-lived sessions (context reuse for multi-turn).
- Warmup: please confirm if production has significant cold-starts (model loads) during that 30-min window; we'll include controlled cold-start runs to quantify load-time impact.
- Client-side instrumentation: send the client-side request_received and final_token timestamps. We will correlate those with server emission timestamps to produce E2E p95/p99.

Ben — can you own the test harness config? Suggested test nodes: 10 clients from our west region pool, TLS + HTTP/2 streaming enabled, and a synthetic mixture: 70% chat-interactive, 30% batch classify. I'll draft the harness and post to the Drive link Kimberly included.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E SLO scoping for Acme Labs — next steps and test scoping

Thanks Marissa — and Daniel, thanks for the PDF and confirmation. Quick plan and calendar items: 

1) Scoping call (30m) — propose Wed 19 May 2027, 10:00–10:30 PDT to finalize traffic mix and IP whitelist. I'll send the invite; please confirm.
2) Deliverables we will provide after the run: 
   - A short report (2–3 pages) with p50/p95/p99 comparisons, a heatmap of tail variance across AZs, and a short appendix listing test harness config and raw CSV results.
   - A short prioritized list of risk mitigations if Redwood misses p99 on any flow (e.g., autoscale knob, pre-warm, model-variant fallback).
3) Internal owners: Ben will create the harness and schedule the runs; Marissa will own instrumentation and report generation; Kimberly will coordinate access and scheduling with your ops.

Action items (owners/due):
- Daniel: upload the 30-min sample JSONL to the Drive (Due: EOD today) — (owner: Acme)
- Daniel: send staging IP whitelist for test clients (Due: tomorrow)
- Ben: draft harness and share a short runbook in Drive (Due: EOD tomorrow)
- Marissa: confirm warmup strategy and cold-starts to be included (Due: Wed morning)

If that looks good I'll lock the calendar and Ben will post the harness link.

Best,
Kimberly
